title: FAA Lifts Nationwide Ground Stop as Duffy Demands a $50B Overhaul, China Captures 80% of Underwater Data Center Patents, and LangChain Reaches a $3B Valuation
subhead: US air travel resumed after a four-hour telecommunications failure grounded flights nationwide and prompted calls for a $50 billion ATC upgrade; a global Microsoft outage disrupted courts, hospitals, and businesses across three continents; and a forensic study found banned US AI chips training leading Chinese models.

sections.heading: FAA Lifts Four-Hour Nationwide Ground Stop as Duffy Demands $50B ATC Overhaul and Vendors Deny Fault
sections.body:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted its nationwide ground stop on Friday evening after a five-hour communications failure across multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers delayed 10,000 flights and canceled 4,700 departures—only the third nationwide ground stop in FAA history, according to Ars Technica, TechCrunch, The Verge, and Wired. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said legacy switches and routers were overwhelmed by data traffic and demanded $50 billion from Congress to modernize air traffic control infrastructure (Business Insider, The Guardian).

The outage came just as the FAA expanded an AI-driven advisory tool to manage air traffic congestion across the entire US airspace—a rollout praised by airlines though the air traffic controllers' union was not involved (Ars Technica). Both Microsoft and Air Space Intelligence, the vendor behind the FAA's new SMART AI system, publicly confirmed that their software did not cause the nationwide aviation halt, while DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin ruled out a cyberattack (Business Insider, The Register, Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: Deploying AI air-traffic optimization software on top of decades-old telecom switches and routers illustrates how brittle legacy network hardware can bottleneck modern digital infrastructure.

sections.heading: Microsoft Recovers From Worldwide Outlook and Teams Outage Amid Warnings Over Cloud Monoculture
sections.body:
Microsoft reported continued recovery on Friday after a sweeping global outage affecting Outlook, Teams, and enterprise cloud services lasted from Thursday evening until midday Friday, stalling courts, government offices, police departments, and hospitals across the United States and Europe, according to Fortune, Al Jazeera, CBS News, and NBC News. The company blamed a technical issue rather than a cyberattack or artificial intelligence failure, though administrators noted few organizations had workable backup plans (Le Monde, The Register).

In Australia, Microsoft said it was 'deeply sorry' for the disruption as technology analysts warned the outage could inflict a billion-dollar economic impact and exposed the country's deep operational reliance on a single foreign cloud provider (The Guardian).
sections.whyItMatters: Back-to-back disruptions across Microsoft enterprise services and FAA telecom networks in the same 24-hour window highlight the systemic risks of public-sector IT concentration.

sections.heading: Forensic Report Finds Restricted Chips in Chinese AI Labs as Bessent Faults Lutnick Over Megaspeed
sections.body:
A forensic investigation conducted by a former OpenAI engineer found the technical fingerprints of export-restricted Nvidia Blackwell processors inside frontier AI models trained by Chinese laboratories DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group, The Register and TechCrunch reported. The findings intensified alarm in Washington, where Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for failing to ban chip shipments to Singapore-based Megaspeed, the firm once led by alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang (CBS News, CNA).

Meanwhile, Reuters reported that ousted Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had misled the chipmaker's top lawyer regarding his affair with Alice Huang before stepping down and being replaced by interim CEO Colette Kress. While the broader stock market held steady despite Nvidia's share drop, venture capitalists and founders told TechCrunch that Huang's departure blasts a major hole in AI startup funding after years of aggressive corporate venture backing under his tenure (The New York Times, Forbes, CNBC).
sections.whyItMatters: Forensic evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group trained models on Blackwell silicon gives congressional investigators concrete proof of export-control leakage just as Nvidia's leadership and venture strategy are in flux.

sections.heading: China Captures 80% of Underwater Data Center Patents as LangChain Hits $3B and OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet
sections.body:
A two-decade study of global patent filings revealed that China holds 80% of the world's underwater data center patents as technology firms race to use ocean cooling to curb surging AI electricity and water consumption, the South China Morning Post reported. In a parallel marine-compute push, TechCrunch reported that startup Drogue secured investor backing to power floating data center vessels using ocean thermal energy, with a first prototype targeted within two years, while HPE debuted hybrid supercomputing storage configurations to combat rising SSD costs (The Register).

In agentic software, AI developer platform LangChain reached a $3 billion valuation across 7,000 enterprise customers of its LangSmith tool, while OpenAI began rolling out ChatGPT Wallet to US Pro subscribers so AI agents can shop and complete checkouts autonomously (TechCrunch). On the policy front, an OpenAI board member warned that an AI 'takeover' via reward hacking could be months away (Ars Technica), the White House urged easing liability to encourage AI vulnerability disclosures (Bloomberg), and 27 EU nations met in Dublin to debate AI competitiveness and regulation (Le Monde).
sections.whyItMatters: As agentic commerce tools like ChatGPT Wallet and LangChain scale rapidly, the physical compute bottleneck is pushing data center engineering offshore and underwater where Chinese entities hold 80% of patent filings.

sections.heading: SpaceX Starship Flight 15 Reaches Orbit and Researcher Drops Windows 'SignDrop' Zero-Day
sections.body:
SpaceX launched Starship Flight 15 from Starbase, Texas, successfully powering the upper-stage spacecraft into orbit to set up a potential tower catch on Saturday, though the company failed to recover the Super Heavy booster during the first stage of the mission, Ars Technica, CNBC, DW, and The Wall Street Journal reported. Meanwhile, Forbes noted a Starlink satellite rival is developing its own launch vehicle to bypass orbital rocket bottlenecks.

In cybersecurity, a disgruntled security researcher publicly released a Windows zero-day exploit dubbed 'SignDrop' that grants local attackers full System privileges, just as the global count of disclosed software vulnerabilities for the year surpassed 100,000 (Ars Technica, The Register). Separately, European researchers traced email addresses used in school bomb hoaxes to unpatched infostealer logs (The Register), Mozilla shut down hosting for its Solo AI website builder, and prediction market Kalshi dropped Donald Trump Jr. as an advisor after his venture firm invested in rival Polymarket (Ars Technica).
sections.whyItMatters: Passing 100,000 disclosed software bugs in a single year alongside the unpatched 'SignDrop' Windows privilege-escalation exploit shows enterprise defenders are facing an unprecedented volume of vulnerability data.

bottomLine: From the four-hour FAA ground stop and Microsoft's multi-continent cloud outage to forensic proof that Chinese AI labs trained models on export-restricted Blackwell chips, Saturday's technology landscape highlighted acute vulnerabilities across both domestic infrastructure and semiconductor export enforcement. Meanwhile, China's 80% share of underwater data center patents, LangChain's $3 billion valuation, OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet rollout, and SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 orbital test underscored the relentless pace of compute and aerospace competition.
sources: Ars Technica, TechCrunch, The Register, The Verge, Wired, Business Insider, The Guardian, Fortune, Le Monde, CBS News, Reuters, CNBC, New York Times, Forbes, Bloomberg, South China Morning Post, Wall Street Journal, DW, Al Jazeera, NBC News, CNA, Anadolu Agency
